newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest seen dry through Friday - Smith Barney.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest seen dry through Friday - Smith Barney.

text.p: Much of the U.S. Midwest should stay fair and dry through Friday, with the next chance for rain seen on Saturday and Sunday, according to a forecast from Jon Davis, meteorologist with Smith Barney in Chicago.

"That chance (for rain) is associated with a cold front that will be moving into the (western Corn) Belt on Saturday and Sunday and then push across the central and western Midwest on Monday and into early Tuesday," Davis' forecast said.
Rainfall coverage from that system is seen at 70 percent for the western Corn Belt and 50 percent for the eastern Corn Belt, the forecast said.

In both halves of the Corn Belt, the chance for rain will be greater in the northern regions. Rainfall amounts are expected to be .3 to 1.5 inches in the Western Corn Belt and .25 to 1.3 inches in the East, the forecast said.
High temperatures on Wednesday were expected to range from 75 to 85 degrees Fahrenheit, and temperatures on Friday were seen climbing to 80 to 89 degrees, the forecast said.
Temperatures over the weekend will begin warming with highs forecast from 82 to 92 degrees Fahrenheit on Saturday, with the warmest temperatures seen in the Western Corn Belt.
